tagline: Through the Chippewa forest, in lady slipper country.
intro: County Road 39 leaves Blackduck and runs south for 28 miles through the pine and hardwood of the Chippewa National Forest, past fishing lakes and an old CCC camp, across the Mississippi and on to US 2 just east of Cass Lake. Lady slippers are a common sight along it.
Blackduck itself was founded in 1900 for the timber. The Laurentian Divide runs near it and drains the land well, and dry land made for good logging.
season: Plan around the lady slipper bloom, which begins in late June.

moments.title: Blackduck
moments.text: Named for Blackduck Lake, the town has the Blue Ox Trail running through it on an old rail line that crosses a railway bridge listed on the National Register.

moments.title: Rabideau CCC Camp
moments.text: Built from 1935 for about 300 young men working in the forest, the camp keeps 13 of its 25 buildings, the mess hall and five barracks among them.
